packet.headline_seed: Toy Story 5 shows 'terror' of children's screen addiction, says Tom Hanks
packet.description_seed: The latest film sees Woody, Buzz and the other toys compete with a new tablet for children's attention.

what: Toy Story 5 shows 'terror' of children's screen addiction, says Tom Hanks

clean_source_blocks.text: US actor Tom Hanks has said the latest Toy Story film highlights children's addiction to screens, an issue that he says strikes "terror in the heart". The fifth instalment of the animated franchise sees Woody, Buzz and Jessie threatened by a new frog-like tablet known as Lilypad, which captivates the film's children. Hanks said the cast related to the storyline because they had all "met that disinterest" of young people who "look down at their phone, look up, look down, look up". "This is a generational thing," he told the BBC's David Sillito, "where one generation has this thing that defines them technologically in society, and they pour everything into it."
The latest film sees Woody, Buzz and the other toys compete with a new tablet for children's attention.

It's a battleground that parents everywhere will recognise, and the film comes at a time of wider debate about the potential harms of too much screen time, particularly social media. Allen, who voices Buzz Lightyear, recalled how he recently took his teenage daughter to the cinema, but she struggled to concentrate for the whole film because children "are so used to seven-second movies on Instagram", he said. His daughter dismissed the film they were watching early on, Allen explained, because she'd already got the gist of what was going to happen. "She actually looked at a motion picture and went, 'I get it! He's going to be the villain and they're going to do this'," he recalled.

"You put a rubber hat on top of a rubber head again and again and again and again, something's gonna chafe," Hanks says. "So, yeah, he does have… let's say a worn area on the back of his head." During the events of Toy Story 4 (2019), Hanks' Woody went off into the sunset to be a hero to abandoned toys. Now in Toy Story 5 (in theaters June 19), he returns to the fold when Jessie (Joan Cusack) and the gang in Bonnie's room are faced with an unbeatable threat: technology. Bonnie's parents gift their daughter (Scarlett Spears) a Lilypad (Greta Lee), a smart device that often wins the battle for the 8-year-old's attention. It's a story inspired by that time in everyone's life when we're told it's no longer cool to play with toys.

payload.title: Tom Hanks: Toy Story 5 tarttuu lasten ruuturiippuvuuden pelkoon
payload.summary: Toy Story 5 -elokuvassa Woody, Buzz, Jessie ja muut lelut joutuvat kilpailemaan lasten huomiosta uuden Lilypad-tabletin kanssa. Tom Hanksin mukaan tarina osuu laajempaan sukupolvikeskusteluun lasten ruutuajasta.
payload.content:
Tom Hanksin mukaan Toy Story 5 käsittelee lasten kiintymystä ruutuihin tavalla, joka herättää aikuisissa tunnistettavaa huolta. Elokuvassa Woody, Buzz, Jessie ja muut tutut lelut kohtaavat uuden vastustajan: Lilypad-nimisen, sammakkoa muistuttavan tabletin, joka vie lasten huomion pois leikeistä.

## Lelut kilpailevat tabletin kanssa

Toy Story -sarjan viidennessä osassa teknologia nousee keskeiseksi jännitteeksi. Tarinassa Bonnien vanhemmat antavat tyttärelleen älylaitteen, joka alkaa voittaa taistelun kahdeksanvuotiaan huomiosta. Tämä asettaa lelut tilanteeseen, jossa niiden merkitys lapsen arjessa horjuu.

Hanks, joka ääninäyttelee Woodya, on kuvannut aihetta sukupolvikokemukseksi. Hänen mukaansa jokaisella ajalla on teknologinen ilmiönsä, johon ihmiset suuntaavat voimakkaasti huomiotaan. Näyttelijä sanoi myös, että elokuvan tekijät tunnistivat tilanteen, jossa nuoret katsovat vuoroin puhelinta ja vuoroin ympärilleen, mutta eivät pysähdy kunnolla läsnä olevaan hetkeen.

Elokuva jatkaa myös Woodyn tarinaa Toy Story 4:n jälkeen. Edellisessä elokuvassa Woody lähti omille teilleen auttamaan hylättyjä leluja, mutta uudessa osassa hän palaa muiden luo, kun Bonnien huoneen lelut joutuvat teknologian haastamiksi.

## Ruutuaika on osa laajempaa keskustelua

Elokuvan aihe osuu aikaan, jolloin lasten ruutuajasta ja erityisesti sosiaalisen median vaikutuksista keskustellaan laajasti. Buzz Lightyearia ääninäyttelevä Tim Allen kertoi esimerkin omasta perheestään: hänen teini-ikäisen tyttärensä oli vaikea keskittyä kokonaiseen elokuvaan, koska lyhyet videot olivat totuttaneet nopeaan rytmiin.

Allen kuvasi myös, kuinka hänen tyttärensä koki ymmärtävänsä katsomansa elokuvan suunnan jo varhaisessa vaiheessa. Hänen mukaansa tämä kertoo tavasta, jolla nopeat sisältömuodot voivat muuttaa kärsivällisyyttä ja odotuksia tarinankerrontaa kohtaan.

Toy Story 5:n asetelma ei siis perustu vain leluhahmojen seikkailuun, vaan tuttuun perhetilanteeseen: leikki, elokuva ja läsnäolo joutuvat kilpailemaan jatkuvasti mukana kulkevan laitteen kanssa. Hanksin mukaan juuri tämä tunnistettavuus tekee aiheesta sekä humoristisen että levottomuutta herättävän.
summary_bullets: Toy Story 5:ssä tutut lelut kilpailevat lasten huomiosta Lilypad-tabletin kanssa.
Tom Hanksin mukaan tarina heijastaa sukupolvikokemusta ja aikuisten huolta lasten ruutuihin uppoutumisesta.
Tim Allen liitti aiheen lyhytvideoiden vaikutukseen lasten ja nuorten keskittymiseen.

article.source_text:
US actor Tom Hanks has said the latest Toy Story film highlights children's addiction to screens, an issue that he says strikes "terror in the heart". The fifth instalment of the animated franchise sees Woody, Buzz and Jessie threatened by a new frog-like tablet known as Lilypad, which captivates the film's children. Hanks said the cast related to the storyline because they had all "met that disinterest" of young people who "look down at their phone, look up, look down, look up". "This is a generational thing," he told the BBC's David Sillito, "where one generation has this thing that defines them technologically in society, and they pour everything into it."

The latest film sees Woody, Buzz and the other toys compete with a new tablet for children's attention.

It's a battleground that parents everywhere will recognise, and the film comes at a time of wider debate about the potential harms of too much screen time, particularly social media. Allen, who voices Buzz Lightyear, recalled how he recently took his teenage daughter to the cinema, but she struggled to concentrate for the whole film because children "are so used to seven-second movies on Instagram", he said. His daughter dismissed the film they were watching early on, Allen explained, because she'd already got the gist of what was going to happen. "She actually looked at a motion picture and went, 'I get it! He's going to be the villain and they're going to do this'," he recalled.

"You put a rubber hat on top of a rubber head again and again and again and again, something's gonna chafe," Hanks says. "So, yeah, he does have… let's say a worn area on the back of his head." During the events of Toy Story 4 (2019), Hanks' Woody went off into the sunset to be a hero to abandoned toys. Now in Toy Story 5 (in theaters June 19), he returns to the fold when Jessie (Joan Cusack) and the gang in Bonnie's room are faced with an unbeatable threat: technology. Bonnie's parents gift their daughter (Scarlett Spears) a Lilypad (Greta Lee), a smart device that often wins the battle for the 8-year-old's attention. It's a story inspired by that time in everyone's life when we're told it's no longer cool to play with toys.
